messages:
jeff_support: FYI QuarkLabs hitting sustained 429s and TPS SLO violations on their Dedicated pool (dedicated-eu-west-2-quark). Started ~10m ago, reports spike then steady throttles. They say burst credits dropped to 0 and some requests are returning 401 intermittently. Can we triage? 

alex_eng: Ack. Do we have metrics/alerts? any autoscaler errors?

sre-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-throttle:dropped_burst_credits{pool=\"dedicated-eu-west-2-quark\"} >= 1 for 5m. admission_controller.rejects increased 3x.

maria_infra: Looking at autoscaler logs — saw scale-up jobs queued, but kube-scheduler backpressure caused worker startup lag ~45s. Also seeing frequent preemptions on the spot nodes.

jeff_support: Logs from customer side show mixed 401/429. They used the same API key for some bursts and a rotated key for others. Snippet: 
```
2024-06-12T14:03:21Z request_id=abc123 status=401 error=\"invalid_token\"
2024-06-12T14:03:22Z request_id=abc124 status=429 error=\"pool_throttled\"
2024-06-12T14:03:23Z request_id=abc125 status=429 error=\"burst_credits_exhausted\"
```

sam_oncall: Repro plan: 1) run a synthetic burst against dedicated-eu-west-2-quark in staging; 2) tail admission_controller + autoscaler logs; 3) check token accounting table for auth failures. On it now.

alex_eng: Command to check burst credit balance quickly: 
```
kubectl exec -n redwood controller -- /usr/local/bin/poolctl credit-balance --pool dedicated-eu-west-2-quark
```
I also recommend checking Prometheus: 
```
sum(rate(admission_controller_rejects_total{pool=\"dedicated-eu-west-2-quark\"}[1m])) by (reason)
```

emily_billing: Noting billing side — if burst credits are exhausted due to a billing sync delay it can look like quota exhaustion. I see an invoice retry for QuarkLabs succeeded 9m ago. Credits should have topped up but the refill job may be delayed. Confirming with billing job logs.

nina_pfe: Customer mentions some requests sub-second that include large batched prompts; they may be consuming more tokens than expected which finishes their credits faster. Asking for their prompt size distribution.

jeff_support: Customer perk: \"we only saw this after deploying a background fanout job — ~15 rps sustained with occasional spikes to 120 rps\". That fits token drain.

sam_oncall: I pushed a temporary admission override to allow +20% headroom for this pool (admission.override=+20%) while we stabilize autoscale. Also bumped prewarm to 2 extra nodes. Monitoring tailing logs.

maria_infra: Autoscaler backlog resolved after nodes came up. Preemption still noisy — filing infra ticket to pin instance class for this pool.

alex_eng: Quick mitigation checklist for support to follow with customer: 
- Reduce client burst rate or add local retry/backoff. 
- Rotate to a fallback compatible model variant with lower tokens/sec cost. 
- Confirm API key used (401s might be from their rotated key hitting older endpoints). 
- We will coordinate a scheduled buffer refill if billing job delayed.

jeff_support: Customer notified and will throttle their fanout for 30m and confirm key. They asked if we can provide steps to validate token-accounting — can we drop a quick query?

alex_eng: Use this SQL to verify their token accounting window: 
```
SELECT account_id, sum(tokens_used) as tokens, min(ts) as start, max(ts) as end
FROM token_usage
WHERE account_id='acct_quark' AND ts > now()- interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY account_id;
```

emily_billing: Billing refill job shows a 7m lag due to a transient db lock — credits were queued and applied at t+9m, which matches customer timeline. I'll follow up with ops to harden.

jeff_support: Great. Closing loop: temporary override + prewarm got them back under SLO, customer to throttle for 30m, billing refill confirmed. Follow-ups: infra pin instance class, billing job retry hardening, and product to add a visible credit-refill timestamp in Console for Dedicated pools. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
